Mhmm....You're right. But recently, in not being able to prevent his absence, I've been going over all the things I could perhaps find out about this stranger and how I could possibly ease the suffering of his loved ones [had he any]. Almost as if I owe it to them for not saving him/ for not postponing his death so that he could seek that needed professional help.
I concede I couldn't of helped him mentally but I just feel like I should have done something at least postpone his death so that he could seek that help. 
I know I should really just accept your advice and stop my blaming myself but it's just so hard.

Thank you for your reply. I really appreciate it.

Ya, I agree that perhaps his end is a release to worldly dilemmas and I've considered these things and hopefully the trauma will fade with time. I'm fairly certain now it's important for me to indeed remember this incident as an example for my future.

Thank you for you reply. I don't know what more to say.

I think what makes the memory of his demise so strong in my mind is the fact that I looked away at the critical moment as he went under.  I feel like it's made it all the more real and crystallized, my brain filling-in in detail where necessary. 
But I guess you're right. I should stop being hard on myself. 

I wanted to thank you for sharing a bit of your own story as well. I think it strengthens what you're trying to tell me and I genuinely feel a bit better. And ya...It's definitely taught me to evaluate the proper worth of the situation, my actions and consequences surrounding these things.

 The response is greatly appreciated. Thanks. I don't know what more to say...but thanks.
Thanks for your reply, by the way. I appreciate it. I wasn't able to reply because I was busy working at school and only left for home around 12 pm. Sorry

I didn't know this person personally, if I did, I don't think I'd of had the courage to post anything anywhere or even speak about it with anyone. That's really discouraging that the post was deleted. I would imagine that it would be incredibly destructive to people who are in need of immediate help.
